sentences.text: Lisa T. Su is chair and chief executive officer of Advanced Micro Devices and also serves on the company's board of directors.

She joined AMD in January 2012 as senior vice president and general manager, global business units, responsible for driving end-to-end business execution of AMD's products and solutions, later serving as chief operating officer, where she unified AMD's business units, sales, operations, and infrastructure into a single organization, before becoming CEO in October 2014 and adding the chair role in 2022.

sentences.quote: Born in Taiwan, Su grew up in Queens, New York. After earning bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees in electrical engineering from MIT, she worked at Texas Instruments, IBM, and Freescale Semiconductor, then joined AMD in 2012.
sentences.text: Born in Taiwan and raised in Queens, New York, she earned bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees in electrical engineering from MIT, and worked at Texas Instruments, IBM, and Freescale Semiconductor before AMD.

sentences.quote: As Chair and CEO of AMD, she has led the company's transformation into a global leader in high performance computing and a key supplier of advanced AI chips.

mgmt_bio.text: Born in Taiwan and raised in Queens, New York, she earned bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees in electrical engineering from MIT, and worked at Texas Instruments, IBM, and Freescale Semiconductor before AMD. As chair and CEO she has led AMD's transformation into a global leader in high performance computing and a key supplier of advanced AI chips.

Board turnover was the main change: McClure was added as a ninth director in January 2026, and Joe Householder, a director since 2014, retired on 19 August 2026, when Tim Ryan joined, McClure became chair of the audit and finance committee and lead independent director Nora Denzel joined it.

sentences.quote: Su has since overseen one of the most remarkable turnarounds in tech, guiding AMD from near-bankruptcy to the cutting edge of the industry.
sentences.text: Lisa Su has been AMD's president and CEO since October 2014, a role she has held since October 2014, and she is now also the company's chair; Stanford GSB characterises her tenure as one of tech's most remarkable turnarounds, guiding AMD from near-bankruptcy to the cutting edge of the industry.

On capital allocation, the board approved a new $6 billion buyback in May 2025, lifting total authority to $14 billion; 12 million shares were repurchased for $1.3 billion during 2025, with $9.4 billion remaining at 27 December 2025.

In October 2025 AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million shares at $0.01, vesting against Instinct GPU purchase milestones and stock-price targets, a dilution-linked structure governance-focused investors may wish to examine.

sentences.text: AMD's Data Center segment set a record in the second quarter of 2026 at $6.7 billion, up 107% year over year on demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs, lifting the segment to 58% of total revenue from about 42% a year earlier.

sentences.quote: Q3 2026 revenue is expected to be approximately $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, representing 41% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
sentences.text: Management guides third-quarter 2026 revenue to roughly $13 billion, about 41% growth year over year, and expects Data Center revenue to more than double in 2027 with server revenue up more than 70%.

A definitive agreement makes AMD a core strategic compute partner to OpenAI for 6 gigawatts of Instinct GPUs, beginning with a 1 gigawatt MI450 deployment in the second half of 2026, with a warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares vesting as purchases scale.

thesis_pillars.text: AMD's Data Center segment set a record in the second quarter of 2026 at $6.7 billion, up 107% year over year on demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs, lifting the segment to 58% of total revenue from about 42% a year earlier. Management guides third-quarter 2026 revenue to roughly $13 billion, about 41% growth year over year, and expects Data Center revenue to more than double in 2027 with server revenue up more than 70%. Additional anchor commitments include a partnership with Anthropic covering up to two gigawatts of Instinct GPUs.
